newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms want hold on trade liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms want hold on trade liberalisation.

text.p: Yugoslav businessmen urged delay of trade liberalisation to protect the economy exhausted by years of sanctions, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported on Wednesday.

"Trade liberalisation regulations prepared by government should conform to World Trade Organisation (WTO) demands but should also take into account that the sanctions-exhausted Yugoslav economy cannot bear international competition at this time," businessmen were quoted as saying.
Liberalisation should be gradual, not abrupt, said the businessmen who were attending the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce industry committee meeting.
Domestic firms needed a two to three year "time out" to recover and liberalisation should adjust to the reality on the ground to prevent it doing more damage than good, they said.
Firms are not opposed to import and export liberalisation but insisted it should be accompanied by regulations to protect the market from bad products and dumping prices.

Producers of sheet glass, cars, chemicals, leather accessories and other products warn of the need to adopt mechanisms to control quality, standard, antidumping prices and other regulations to protect the domestic market, in keeping with similar measures of the WTO and the European Union. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
